notes: Cleanup car: inbound polling health plus three fully isolated E2E harnesses - the last two engineering-debt items on the list. Inbound health: every channel route now keeps a tiny atomic health sidecar next to its cursor (<state>/channels/<route>.health with last-ok, last-fail and consecutive-failure stamps); a successful poll zeroes the counter, a failed poll increments it, a health write failure logs one sanitized line and never breaks the poll, and a corrupt or missing file reads as honest unknown. GET /api/channels rows gain inbound_health with healthy (null = never polled, not a fake failure), last-ok age and cursor presence; the console channel rows show the new status line - gray 'not polled yet', green 'ok - 12s ago', amber 'ok but no cursor yet', red 'failing x3' - and hide the whole line when the field is absent. Harness isolation: e2e_channels, e2e_channels_dom and e2e_car4a no longer touch production secrets or settings at all - they copy byte-identical snapshots into throwaway per-leg profiles with sentinel credentials, spawn their own consoles on ports 8921-8923, and keep production byte-identity purely as a teardown assertion with no restore path (there is nothing left to restore). Counts grew with the guard: 8/44/35 to 12/46/39, all green. Gates after this car: core 1498/1498 (+21 health legs), console smoke 234/234, router 30/30, memory 58/58, setup 99/99, profile 63/63, desktop 15/15, source lint 0/67 + packs 658 to 662, publish gate READY(0), the 17-leg E2E series green with the three migrated harnesses re-run serially, site gates 62 + 59, screenshots 7/7; docs counts synced (channels 12/46, car4a 39); core 29 modules ~15.4k LOC.
